subject: Acme — feature parity: streaming + tool-calls follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jared Thompson <jared@acme.com>; Tanya Ruiz <tanya@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme — feature parity: streaming + tool-calls follow-up

Thanks again for the time today — great to see the team’s priorities for the support UX and real-time assistance use cases. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

1) What we heard
- Primary goal: reduce perceived latency on chat assistant and support triage while preserving structured outputs for downstream systems (JSON schemas).
- Must-haves: streaming token-level responses, deterministic function/tool calling with structured outputs, and auditability for compliance.
- Evaluation constraints: need a head-to-head on throughput/latency against the hyperscaler endpoint you mentioned, and a sample of your support snippets to validate entity extraction accuracy.

2) Proposed tests (attached: acme-maf-eval-plan.pdf)
- Streaming latency: measure first-token and tail latency at 1, 5, 25 concurrent users; sequences 64/256/1024 tokens.
- Function calling correctness: run 200 prompts that trigger tool calls; validate schema adherence and error rates.
- Structured output fidelity: compare JSON schema fields against ground truth from your dataset.
- Competitor baseline: run same tests against HyperscaleAI inference API and report deltas (latency, cost per 1k tokens, failure modes).

3) Logistics / timeline
- Please share the sample dataset (snippets) and an NDA if needed.
- Rishi will run an initial streaming + function-calling pilot and share a short report within 3 business days of receiving the data.
- Booked a follow-up sync (optional) on May 5; if that works for you we’ll turn the pilot into a live demo.

Next steps for you:
- Share the support snippets CSV and any existing prompt lists (Tanya?)
- Confirm whether you want Redwood hosted endpoints or a Dedicated evaluation (we can do both; Dedicated gives more parity on latency).

Appended a short internal note for Rishi on the test plan and a Drive link with the evaluation matrix: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C_redwood-acme-eval

Thanks — talk soon.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0187

Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — feature parity: streaming + tool-calls follow-up

Marissa — thanks for the recap and clear plan. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- We attached a small sample of anonymized support snippets (acme-support-snippets.csv) for the initial run. This is ~1.2k rows and should be enough to validate entity extraction and structured outputs.
- On model selection: we’re flexible. For the first pass we’d like you to run Redwood hosted + HyperscaleAI baseline. If Dedicated shows better tail latency we’ll consider that for the POC.
- Procurement/Timeline: procurement wants an estimate of scope/cost before May 12 to align the budget. Not a hard stop but helpful.

Also: would you be able to include a simple throughput test (RPS at 95th pct latency) so procurement can see cost tradeoffs?

Cc’ing Tanya for dataset handoff. I’ll send NDA if you need one — otherwise we’re fine with this snippet.

— Jared

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — feature parity: streaming + tool-calls follow-up

Thanks Jared — got the sample CSV and the ask. Quick technical plan and proposed test matrix (I’ll run the first pass once you confirm access):

1) Streaming latency tests (Redwood hosted vs HyperscaleAI)
- First-byte latency, 95/99 tail measured at 1/5/25 concurrent users
- Sequence lengths: 64, 256, 1024 tokens
- Payloads: your snippets with prompt framing for support triage (I’ll attach the exact prompts)

2) Function/tool calling
- We’ll instrument 200 prompts designed to trigger the tools you described (ticket-create, user-lookup).
- Validation: schema conformance (JSON Schema), success rate, and any partial/streamed-tool-call failure modes.

3) Structured outputs & fidelity
- Map ground-truth fields from your CSV to target JSON fields; compute precision/recall per field and a composite pass rate.

4) Throughput/cost sweep for procurement
- RPS sweep at 50/200/500 RPS until 95th pct latency > target (250ms first-byte target for streaming).
- I’ll capture token counts to estimate cost per 1k tokens for Redwood vs HyperscaleAI using your typical prompt+response sizes.

Attachments: redwood-streaming-test-plan.json (stubbed), benchmark-script.sh (small harness). I’ll run an initial 50-prompt pass today and send results by EOD tomorrow. If we see an obvious delta we’ll schedule a short engineering deep-dive.

Let me know if you want us to provision a Dedicated eval (rough ETA 48 hrs) — Dedicated will remove noisy multi-tenant tail-effects and give the closest parity to on-prem.

— Rishi

Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
